passage: Do all bats rely on echolocation for navigation? Dr. Jada Ware and her research team argue that fruit bats originally used echolocation, but that they abandoned this method over 40 million years ago as they adapted to daytime foraging. After analyzing bat fossils and DNA sequences, the scientists determined that fruit bats gradually developed enhanced color vision, larger brain regions for visual processing, and different wing structures better suited for daylight flight than sound-based navigation. Therefore, dietary preferences may have driven these bats to shift from echolocation to visual navigation.
